solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Device for measuring space time

parts.note: the space is a spot for a car at the kerb, and the device times how long a driver may leave it there

explanation.surface: Sounds like a physicist's instrument for gauging space-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space time' suggests Einstein's spacetime; here it is the time allowed in a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerbside coin machine records paid time for a parked car in its bay.

clue.text: Guidance on washing machine use, perhaps for mum!

definitions.text: Guidance on washing machine use, perhaps for mum!

parts.words: Guidance on washing machine use, perhaps for mum!
parts.note: literally an instruction to load hosiery into the drum; as an idiom it is a rude order to be quiet, and mum means silent

explanation.surface: A laundry tip that a helpful child might give to their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase is a blunt British command to shut up, i.e. to go mum.

clue.text: Short African mammal by eastern river

indicators.note: short means the animal's name is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a rhino is a large African mammal

explanation.surface: A stubby beast found beside an eastern waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Non-believer in force led one to change direction

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: changing direction means the words led and one are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unbeliever commanding a troop forced it to turn about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change direction' turns LED + I into IDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone without religious faith, as seen by followers of a particular creed.

clue.text: Attempt revolution, rising against new command

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: rev is short for a revolution of an engine

explanation.surface: Rebels plan an uprising against a fresh order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns REV into VER in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or have authority over, a verb synonym of command.

clue.text: Reformed loner to join society?

indicators.note: reformed means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A recluse who has changed their ways signs up to mix with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up as a member, as one might with a club or society.

clue.text: When speaking, I cut facial hair

indicators.note: when speaking means the pronoun is heard rather than read, so it becomes the organ of sight

parts.note: the pronoun I is pronounced exactly like the organ of sight
to lash is to cut with a whip

explanation.surface: Someone admits, as they talk, to trimming their beard.
explanation.definitionFit: A single hair growing on the edge of the eyelid is a hair on the face.

clue.text: Tracy recalls misbehaving with absolute lucidity

indicators.note: misbehaving means the letters act up and fall into disorder

explanation.surface: Tracy remembers her bad behaviour in perfect detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crystal-clear is entirely transparent and easy to understand, i.e. lucid without doubt.

clue.text: Criminal husband shown in dodgy E-FIT

indicators.note: shown in means the letter appears inside the rearranged picture's letters
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police release an unconvincing photofit of a married lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges EFIT into TIEF, and 'shown in' puts H inside. An E-FIT is a computer-built likeness of a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a person who steals, one particular kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Revere bust bringing in millions for artist

indicators.note: bringing in means the rearranged letters take a letter inside them
bust means broken, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A sculpted head of Paul Revere sells for a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' rearranges REVERE into VEREER, and 'bringing in' puts M inside. 'Bust' looks like sculpture, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: South bank is narrow

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money

explanation.surface: A riverbank in the south is only a thin strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverside, but here it is a financial lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means thin or of small width, a synonym of narrow.

clue.text: Charges a lot

definitions.meaning: puts cargo into, as one charges a gun or a lorry

explanation.surface: Someone billing heavily for their services.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is charged by being filled; and informally lots and lots means a great deal.

clue.text: Chess piece lieutenant put back in box

indicators.note: in means the reversed pair goes inside the container word

parts.note: a case is a box

indicators.note: put back means the abbreviation is placed in reverse order

explanation.surface: An officer returns a chess piece to its storage box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns LT into TL, which goes 'in' CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook in chess is also commonly called by the name of a fortified building.

clue.text: Fanatics surrounding area turned on church faithful

indicators.note: turned means the combined letters are read backwards
surrounding means the fanatics' word goes around the letter for area

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts or fanatics, as in sports nuts

explanation.surface: Zealots in a district have turned against the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts A in NUTS for NUATS; 'turned' gives STAUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means loyal and committed, a synonym of faithful.

clue.text: Crack a maths problem with inspiration?

indicators.note: to crack is to break, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Solving a mathematical puzzle needs a flash of insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like solve, but signals the anagram; 'inspiration' means breathing in, not a bright idea.
explanation.definitionFit: This lung condition causes wheezing and makes breathing in difficult, a respiratory ailment.

clue.text: Part of Indonesia shown in retrospective series from Jakarta museum

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read in reverse
shown in means the letters are on display inside the words Jakarta museum

explanation.surface: An Indonesian island features in a retrospective exhibition from a Jakarta gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'jakARTA MUSeum' gives the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large island in western Indonesia.

clue.text: Perhaps Pluto and friend upset Chihuahua, say

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Pluto is a cartoon dog in Disney films

explanation.surface: Mickey's dog and a companion annoy a tiny Mexican breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chihuahua is a small pampered pet dog of the kind kept on a lap.

clue.text: Picture that is on outside of magazine

indicators.note: on outside of means the pair of letters wrap around the abbreviated periodical

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A photograph on a periodical's front cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a representation or likeness, a synonym of picture.

clue.text: Elegant white bird: for example, tailless tern ascending

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: in a down entry ascending means the letters read upwards, i.e. reversed
tailless means the seabird's final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A graceful pale seabird, a tern perhaps, flies up without its tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' leaves TER and 'ascending' turns it to RET.
explanation.definitionFit: This heron is a slender long-legged wading bird with snowy plumage.

clue.text: Book of dates and times kept by signalman accurately

indicators.note: kept by means the letters are held within the words signalman accurately

explanation.surface: A railway signalman keeps a precise logbook of train times.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual calendar listing dates, tides, sunrise times and other events.

clue.text: Nick's incomplete comment on chapter

definitions.note: Nick's stands for nick is: a nick is a small cut

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the comment word is dropped

parts.note: a note is a brief comment

explanation.surface: Nick's remark on a chapter is left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick in a surface.

clue.text: I blush after accepting name is disregarded

indicators.note: after means the blushing phrase follows the single letter
accepting means the blushing phrase takes the letter for name inside it

parts.note: to go red is to blush

explanation.surface: Someone flushes with embarrassment after being snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts N inside GO RED for GNORED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ignored is to be overlooked or paid no attention, the same as being disregarded.

clue.text: It is included in the donation

indicators.note: included in means the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is part of the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of income given to the church, a kind of donation.

clue.text: Visual artist confusing Hopper with Hogarth almost

indicators.note: confusing means the combined letters are muddled up into a new order
almost means the painter's surname loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An art critic mixes up the painters Edward Hopper and William Hogarth.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer creates pictures with a camera, so is a visual artist.
